final_candidates.decision_summary: K41 is a known acetylation site in the activation domain; K-to-R preserves charge while blocking acetylation, a plausible modulator of Tat transactivation. Highest mutant frequency (0.151) among K-to-R candidates supports evolutionary tolerance.

Full MSA coverage with mutant frequency 0.116 and the best PLM score among K-to-R candidates; K29 lies in the core region influencing CycT1 binding. Conservative substitution minimizes viability risk.
K50 is an acetylation site in the TAR-binding basic region; removing acetylation while retaining positive charge could enhance transactivation, though low MSA tolerance (0.02) tempers confidence.

stop_reason.detail: No remaining applicable tool measures transactivation directly; existing MSA/PLM evidence plus domain knowledge already stabilizes the Top-3 ranking.

history.rationale: Lys41 lies between the cysteine-rich core and basic domain; conservative K->R preserves charge and is commonly tolerated, potentially tuning core/ARM folding for stronger TAR/cyclinT1 interaction.
Conservative Lys->Arg in the basic RNA-binding domain; likely preserves TAR binding while subtly altering transactivation. No evidence yet, so retained pending MSA/PLM data.

Highest mutant frequency (0.151) among all candidates in a key activation-domain residue; K41 is acetylated in WT and Arg substitution is known to modulate transactivation. PLM score is low but PLM is only a generic plausibility prior, not a transactivation measure.
Lys50 in the basic (ARM/TAR-binding) domain; K->R preserves positive charge while altering H-bonding geometry, and is evolutionarily common in HIV-1 isolates, plausibly enhancing RNA binding.
K50 acetylation site in the basic domain; K->R blocks acetylation and can modulate Tat transactivation; retained pending evidence.

K50 in the TAR-binding basic region is an acetylation site; K-to-R removes acetylation while preserving charge, a plausible transactivation modulator, but MSA tolerance is low (0.02), so confidence is reduced.
Lys51 is another basic-domain residue; conservative arginine swap may improve TAR RNA affinity without disrupting the core structure.
Adjacent basic-domain lysine; conservative substitution with possible effect on P-TEFb interaction; retained.
Adjacent acetylation site to K50 with similar rationale but equally low MSA tolerance; kept as backup with reduced confidence.
Lys28 in the Cys-rich domain; conservative substitution could modulate metal coordination environment and cyclinT1 binding while remaining charge-conservative.
K28 acetylation site regulating Tat-CyclinT1 interaction; K->R may increase transactivation; retained pending evidence.
Zero mutant frequency across 69 fully covering homologs and near-zero PLM score indicate strong purifying constraint at K28 (Cys-rich/core boundary); dropped.

rejection.reason: Zero mutant frequency across 69 fully covering homologs and near-zero PLM score indicate strong purifying constraint at K28 (Cys-rich/core boundary); dropped.

history.rationale: Lys29 adjacent to K28; charge-preserving change with potential effect on core-domain packing and transactivation complex stability.
Adjacent to K28; similar acetylation-site rationale; retained.
Promoted to rank 2: full MSA coverage with mutant frequency 0.116 and the best PLM score (0.104) among K-to-R candidates; K29 sits in the core region influencing CycT1 binding.
Arg56 in the basic domain; R->K retains charge and is seen in natural variants, possibly fine-tuning TAR bulge recognition.
Conservative swap at end of basic domain; possible RNA-affinity tuning; retained as mid-priority candidate.
R56 is part of the invariant GRKKRRQRRR ARM essential for TAR RNA binding; even conservative R-to-K risks disrupting RNA recognition and shows low MSA/PLM support.

rejection.reason: R56 is part of the invariant GRKKRRQRRR ARM essential for TAR RNA binding; even conservative R-to-K risks disrupting RNA recognition and shows low MSA/PLM support.

history.rationale: Asn61 in the glutamine-rich C-terminal region; small polar substitution could enhance solubility/secondary interactions without structural risk.
C-terminal region polymorphic in natural isolates; low prior but cheap to evaluate; retained.
Highest mutant frequency (0.293) and PLM (0.262) of the pool, indicating strong natural tolerance, but position 61 is in a region with weaker direct linkage to transactivation, so kept mid-rank.
C-terminal Glu86; conservative E->D may modestly affect the second exon C-terminus contribution to transactivation.
C-terminal conservative change; likely neutral-to-mild effect on stability; retained as low-priority.
Zero mutant frequency with low coverage and entropy ~0 (position effectively invariant where aligned); no rationale linking it to transactivation gains.

rejection.reason: Zero mutant frequency with low coverage and entropy ~0 (position effectively invariant where aligned); no rationale linking it to transactivation gains.

history.rationale: Lys12 in the acidic proline-rich N-terminus; conservative change with possible effect on cellular factor recruitment.
N-terminal proline-rich region lysine; weak prior; retained to fill evaluation set.
Zero mutant frequency despite full coverage; K12 in the proline-rich N-terminus lacks a clear transactivation-enhancing rationale.

rejection.reason: Zero mutant frequency despite full coverage; K12 in the proline-rich N-terminus lacks a clear transactivation-enhancing rationale.

history.rationale: Gln54 within the basic domain; adding a positive charge could strengthen TAR RNA electrostatic binding, though at higher risk of over-stabilizing nonspecific RNA binding.
Charge addition near basic-domain boundary; speculative; retained for evidence gathering.
Low MSA tolerance (0.022) and near-zero PLM score; adding a positive charge within the basic region offers no clear benefit over the existing ARM.

rejection.reason: Low MSA tolerance (0.022) and near-zero PLM score; adding a positive charge within the basic region offers no clear benefit over the existing ARM.
